review_notes:
I read all 177 lines of the target file. I also read the definitions of `interpolation`, `endpointCoupling`, `IsCoupling` and `QuadraticTransportCost` in Model.lean, and the existing lemmas `endpointCoupling_add`, `quadraticTransportCost_add` and `interpolation_restricted` in TimeHalf.lean. In Mathlib I checked `Measure.map_smul`, which is tagged `@[simp]` but takes an `AEMeasurable` side condition. Grep turned up the same manual proof patterns in other WeakHessian files (OptimalPlansShort, RerouteFiniteSubplanShort, GeodesicPlanSupportedBall, LiftBoundedCoupling).

The file has no simp attributes of its own. Its main simp-interface problem is that `interpolation` and `endpointCoupling` are plain `def`s wrapping `Measure.map`, and they come with no smul or projection lemmas. So Mathlib's simp lemma `Measure.map_smul` never matches them unless the definitions are unfolded with `change` or `simp only [def]`, and its measurability side condition then has to be supplied by hand.

I did not run Lean, so the proposed lemmas and simplified proofs are untested. I only suggest `@[simp]` for lemmas with no hypotheses, which push a scalar outward through a definition; these cannot loop. Degenerate cases (for example c = 0 or c = ∞) need no hypotheses, because both `Measure.map_smul` and `lintegral_smul_measure` hold for every `ℝ≥0∞` scalar.

findings.problem: The term `interpolation (c • π) t` comes up three times in this proof: in `he` (l.94–95), `hξend` (l.140–147) and `hs'` (l.162–166). Its natural normal form is `c • interpolation π t`, but no lemma about `interpolation` gives it. `interpolation` is an opaque `def` for `Measure.map (fun γ => γ t) π`, so Mathlib's `@[simp] Measure.map_smul` does not fire on it. Even after unfolding, simp would still need the `AEMeasurable` side condition. Each time, the proof unfolds with `change`, rewrites with an explicit measurability proof, and folds back with `change`. The same block is copied into OptimalPlansShort.lean, RerouteFiniteSubplanShort.lean and GeodesicPlanSupportedBall.lean.
findings.proposed_change:
Next to `interpolation` (Model.lean), or next to `interpolation_restricted` in TimeHalf.lean, add a lemma with no hypotheses:
```lean
@[simp] lemma interpolation_smul (c : ℝ≥0∞) (π : Measure (Curve X)) (t : Time) :
    interpolation (c • π) t = c • interpolation π t :=
  Measure.map_smul c (continuous_eval_const t).measurable.aemeasurable
```
Then `he t` becomes `interpolation_smul _ _ _`. `hξend` becomes `by simp only [ξ, interpolation_smul, ht, he, smul_smul, ENNReal.mul_inv_cancel hq hqt, one_smul]` or an equivalent `rw` chain. In `hs'`, `simp only [interpolation_smul, Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul] at hs` replaces the `change`/`rw` pair.
findings.benefit: The scalar moves outward to a canonical form that simp can reach without unfolding `interpolation`, so the `change` steps that depend on definitional unfolding go away. All the duplicated call sites across the WeakHessian files could use the same one-line lemma. Orienting it outward matches Mathlib's `Measure.map_smul`, and since the lemma has no hypotheses simp can always apply it.

findings.problem: The proof needs `QuadraticTransportCost (endpointCoupling (q • η)) = q * QuadraticTransportCost (endpointCoupling η)`. It gets this from a local `have hs` that unfolds both definitions and passes `Measure.map_smul` an explicitly built measurability proof. The project already has the additive counterparts `endpointCoupling_add` and `quadraticTransportCost_add`, but no scalar ones. The same `hs` block is copied verbatim into OptimalPlansShort.lean (l.265–270). There is also a `change` on line 151, which only turns `•` into `*` on `ℝ≥0∞`.
findings.proposed_change:
Put two lemmas with no hypotheses beside `endpointCoupling_add` and `quadraticTransportCost_add` in TimeHalf.lean:
```lean
@[simp] lemma endpointCoupling_smul (c : ℝ≥0∞) (π : Measure (Curve X)) :
    endpointCoupling (c • π) = c • endpointCoupling π :=
  Measure.map_smul c ((continuous_eval_const timeZero).measurable.prodMk
    (continuous_eval_const timeOne).measurable).aemeasurable

@[simp] lemma quadraticTransportCost_smul (c : ℝ≥0∞) (q : Measure (X × X)) :
    QuadraticTransportCost (c • q) = c * QuadraticTransportCost q :=
  lintegral_smul_measure _ _
```
Then the local `hs η` becomes `by simp`, or `by rw [endpointCoupling_smul, quadraticTransportCost_smul]`, and the local `have hs` with its `hmeas` can be deleted.
findings.benefit: This completes the existing `_add` API with the matching `_smul` rules, so simp can normalize scalar multiples of transport plans to `c * cost` without unfolding the definitions. A copied block in at least two files is replaced, and readers see a named fact instead of a re-derived one.

findings.problem: `IsCoupling q μ₀ μ₁` is defined as `Measure.map Prod.fst q = μ₀ ∧ Measure.map Prod.snd q = μ₁`. So the expressions `(endpointCoupling π).map Prod.fst` and `(endpointCoupling π).map Prod.snd` come up often, and their natural normal forms are `interpolation π timeZero` and `interpolation π timeOne`. There are no named projection lemmas for this. Instead the proof unfolds both definitions, applies `Measure.map_map` with a local measurability proof `hm`, and relies on `Function.comp_def`. IsOptimalCoupling.reroute_plan in TimeHalf.lean repeats this exact `hm` and `simp only` combination.
findings.proposed_change:
Add projection lemmas with no hypotheses and use them to prove `endpointCoupling_couples` and the TimeHalf proof:
```lean
@[simp] lemma map_fst_endpointCoupling (π : Measure (Curve X)) :
    (endpointCoupling π).map Prod.fst = interpolation π timeZero := by
  simp only [endpointCoupling, interpolation, Measure.map_map measurable_fst
    ((continuous_eval_const timeZero).measurable.prodMk
      (continuous_eval_const timeOne).measurable), Function.comp_def]
```
Add the analogous `map_snd_endpointCoupling` with `timeOne`. Then `endpointCoupling_couples π := ⟨map_fst_endpointCoupling π, map_snd_endpointCoupling π⟩`, and in `reroute_plan` the coupling step becomes `⟨by simpa using hends'.1, by simpa using hends'.2⟩`.
findings.benefit: The link between the two definitions is stated once, in a form simp can use, instead of being rebuilt by unfolding at each use. Downstream goals of the form `IsCoupling (endpointCoupling _) _ _` then reduce by `simp` to equalities between `interpolation` terms, which is the form the rest of the development works in (`interpolation_endpoints`, `he0`, `he1`).
